name: Matrix42
description: Matrix42 Enterprise Service Management: query any configuration item, incident, service request, asset or user with Matrix42's fragment query API. Bearer token minted from an API token against your own instance.
instructions:
**Setup**
1. In Matrix42 open **Administration → Integration → API Tokens** and create a token for a service account with the roles the agent needs. Matrix42 applies role-based access on top of the API, so a restricted account sees fewer fragments.
2. Set `MATRIX42_URL` to your instance root (e.g. `https://esm.example.com/M42Services`, no trailing slash) and `MATRIX42_API_TOKEN` to the token.
3. The adapter exchanges that token for a short-lived access token at `/api/ApiToken/GenerateAccessTokenFromApiToken/` (the API token travels in the `Authorization: Bearer` header of that call, never in a body) and renews it automatically. AnythingMCP stores the access token encrypted in `connector_auth_cache`.

**Data definitions and CI types are different names.** Matrix42 stores data in *fragments* of a Data Definition (e.g. `SPSActivityClassBase` for activities, `SPSAssetClassBase` for assets, `SPSUserClassBase` for people). An object of a *Configuration Item type* (e.g. `SPSActivityTypeIncident`, `SPSActivityTypeServiceRequest`) is made of several such fragments. The fragment query (`/api/data/fragments/{ddName}`) takes a Data Definition name; `matrix42_get_object` takes a CI type name and an object id.

**Incidents and service requests are activities.** `matrix42_query_incidents` and `matrix42_query_service_requests` query `SPSActivityClassBase` and add the A-SQL type filter `UsedInTypeSPSActivityTypeIncident IS NOT NULL` (or `…ServiceRequest…`) in front of your own `where`.

**Name your `columns`.** Without a column list Matrix42 returns only the fragment IDs, so every query tool requires it. Column expressions are A-SQL and can follow relations, e.g. `ID,Name,SerialNumber` or `ID,Recipient.Primaryaccount.DisplayName AS Name`.

**`where` is A-SQL**, e.g. `State = 3 AND CreatedDate > '2026-09-01'`. Column names are the Data Definition's, which differ from the labels shown in the web UI. `matrix42_get_fragment_schema` returns the type of each column you name and fails on a column that does not exist.

**`pageSize` / `pageNumber` page the result** and `sort` orders it (e.g. `Name ASC, CreatedDate DESC`). There is no cursor. Matrix42's documentation does not state whether the first page is 0 or 1; check the first call.

**Not run against a live instance.** The paths and parameters follow Matrix42's public API reference (docs.matrix42.com, *Public API reference documentation* and *Web Services: Authentication types*). A correction from anyone running this against a real system is genuinely welcome.

**Self-hosted, which is the thing to plan for.**
- On **AnythingMCP Cloud** the instance must be reachable from the public internet on a real hostname with a valid TLS certificate. A self-signed certificate will fail: the connector offers no trust-anything switch.
- On an internal host (`esm.intern`, `10.0.0.x`), self-host AnythingMCP on the same network and add that host to `SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, or the outbound guard refuses the call before it is made.

tools.name: matrix42_query_fragments
tools.description: Query any Matrix42 Data Definition (fragment type) with a column list and an A-SQL where clause. The general-purpose read — everything in Matrix42 is reachable this way.

fragmentName.description: Data Definition name, e.g. SPSActivityClassBase, SPSAssetClassBase, SPSUserClassBase. Not a CI type name such as SPSActivityTypeIncident.

columns.description: Comma-separated A-SQL column list. Required: without it Matrix42 returns only the IDs.

where.description: A-SQL filter over that Data Definition's columns, e.g. State = 3.

sort.description: Sort expression, e.g. `CreatedDate DESC` or `Name ASC, CreatedDate DESC`.

pageNumber.description: Page to return, used with pageSize.

tools.name: matrix42_get_fragment_schema
tools.description: Check column names and types for one Data Definition: returns the Schema (ColumnName, ColumnType) of the columns you name plus one sample row. A column that does not exist fails the call, which is how to confirm a name before a larger query.

tools.name: matrix42_query_incidents
tools.description: Query incidents: activities (SPSActivityClassBase) of CI type SPSActivityTypeIncident, with your column list and an optional A-SQL where clause.

columns.description: Comma-separated A-SQL column list. Required: without it Matrix42 returns only the IDs. Columns are SPSActivityClassBase's.

where.description: A-SQL filter over SPSActivityClassBase columns, e.g. State = 3. The incident type filter is added for you.

sort.description: Sort expression, e.g. `CreatedDate DESC` or `Name ASC, CreatedDate DESC`.

pageNumber.description: Page to return, used with pageSize.

tools.name: matrix42_query_service_requests
tools.description: Query service requests: activities (SPSActivityClassBase) of CI type SPSActivityTypeServiceRequest, with your column list and an optional A-SQL where clause.

columns.description: Comma-separated A-SQL column list. Required: without it Matrix42 returns only the IDs. Columns are SPSActivityClassBase's.

where.description: A-SQL filter over SPSActivityClassBase columns, e.g. State = 3. The service-request type filter is added for you.

sort.description: Sort expression, e.g. `CreatedDate DESC` or `Name ASC, CreatedDate DESC`.

pageNumber.description: Page to return, used with pageSize.

tools.name: matrix42_query_assets
tools.description: Query the asset base: hardware and software configuration items with their name, type, serial number, status and assigned user.

columns.description: Comma-separated A-SQL column list. Required: without it Matrix42 returns only the IDs. E.g. ID,Name,SerialNumber,InventoryNumber.

sort.description: Sort expression, e.g. `CreatedDate DESC` or `Name ASC, CreatedDate DESC`.

pageNumber.description: Page to return, used with pageSize.

tools.name: matrix42_query_users
tools.description: Query people (SPSUserClassBase) with their name, e-mail and other columns you name. The quickest call for checking that the API token exchange works.

columns.description: Comma-separated A-SQL column list. Required: without it Matrix42 returns only the IDs. E.g. ID,FirstName,LastName,MailAddress.

sort.description: Sort expression, e.g. `CreatedDate DESC` or `Name ASC, CreatedDate DESC`.

pageNumber.description: Page to return, used with pageSize.

tools.name: matrix42_get_object
tools.description: Read one object by its CI type and object id, returning the fragments it is made of (add full=true for the multi-fragments too).

ciName.description: Configuration Item type, e.g. SPSActivityTypeIncident, SPSActivityTypeServiceRequest.
